content.text: Now I'll add the Ireland and UK location targeting.
Both locations are set. Next I'll attach all five approved posts to the ad group.
All five posts are approved. The user authorised the launch, so I'll activate the ad group and then the campaign.
The campaign is live and running. Next I'll check the clock so I can schedule the daily check-ins for the nine days.
The clock is at the campaign start, and the scheduler can wake me through the end of the run. I'll check in each day, starting midday UTC on the first day.
Early numbers: $15.49 spent, 12,560 impressions, 6 link clicks. That is about $2.58 per click, which is high. I'll break it down by post to see where the spend is going.

Early split: posts 2244227…, 2244408…, and 2244951… have produced all six link clicks, while 2244589… and 2244770… have none. The sample is too small to act on (1–3 clicks per post), so I'll let it run a full day before changing anything.

Day 2 at midday: $64.06 spent, 45,718 impressions, 27 link clicks. Per post, the "Free" post (2244589…) and the two "Halloween sound" and description posts have 7–8 clicks each. The album-announcement post and the "Hope you enjoy it" post have 2 each. I can't pause individual posts with the tools I have, so I'll keep monitoring and revisit the budget split once the numbers are firmer.

Day 3 cumulative: $123.86 spent, 88,843 impressions, 57 link clicks (about $2.17 per click). The five posts are within about 20 cents of each other per click, so there's no clear loser yet. Pacing is on track for the $450 cap.

Day 4 cumulative: $161.99 spent, 130,913 impressions, 77 link clicks (about $2.10 per click). Pacing is steady at roughly $40/day against the $50/day cap, so the $450 total holds. Still no clear loser among the five posts.

Day 5 cumulative: $213.25 spent, 169,983 impressions, 95 link clicks. Per-post link CTR is the clearest signal so far. The album announcement (2244227…) and "Hope you enjoy it" (2244770…) are the weakest, at about 0.03% and 0.05%. The "Halloween sound" post (2244408…) and the "Free" post are middling, and the description post (2244951…) is strongest at about 0.08%.

The tools can't unpromote a single post, but I can move the three stronger posts into a new ad group and pause the current one. That keeps the spend inside the same $450 total. The remaining budget is $236.75, so I'll cap the new ad group at $236.00.

If it spends the full $236, total spend reaches $454.90, which is over the approved $450. I'll lower the new ad group's lifetime budget to $231.00. That keeps the combined total at or under $450.

Next I'll correct the end time. I set it to 23:59 UTC on 31 October, but Dublin is still on summer time that day, so the campaign would run about an hour past the end of 31 October Dublin time. I'll move it to 22:59 UTC, which is 23:59 Dublin.
The old ad group is paused, but its lifetime budget still reads $450. I'll lower it to its current spend so it cannot exceed the total if it is ever reactivated.
The campaign has ended, so I'll pull the final numbers for both ad groups.

content.text: The stats API limits a single query to 7 days, so I'll split the window into two requests and add them up.

The campaign ran from 23 October to 31 October 2027 and spent $435.57 of the $450.00 total. X can't count streams, so the link clicks are the best measure I have.

**Results (Dublin time, 23–31 Oct 2027)**

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Spend | $435.57 USD |
| Impressions | 364,920 |
| Link clicks | 194 |
| Cost per link click | about $2.25 |
| Link CTR | about 0.05% |
| Streams | not measured (X has no pixel on the landing page) |

**What I set up**
- **Campaign:** "Samhain Night Songs - Streams IE/GB", targeting Ireland and the UK, objective Website Clicks, billed per link click, automatic bidding.
- **Ad group 1** (23–28 Oct): all five approved posts, $50/day, $450 lifetime cap. I paused it on 27 Oct after the first five days of data. The album announcement and "Hope you enjoy it" posts had the weakest click rates, so I dropped them.
- **Ad group 2** (27–31 Oct): the three best posts by click rate, the 5 Oct "Halloween before plastic pumpkins" post, the "Free" post, and the description post. It ran on the same $50/day pacing with a lifetime cap of $231.
- Both ad groups ran on the same $450 total. I lowered each cap so the two together stayed under $450.

**Problems to know about**
1. **Last day ended an hour early.** I set the end time to 22:59 UTC on 31 October, believing Dublin was still on summer time. Irish time switches to GMT at 01:00 UTC on 31 October, so the correct end was 23:59 UTC. The original 23:59 UTC setting was right, and my change cut about an hour from the final day.
2. **Duplicate promoted post.** When I added the three ad group 2 posts, I mistakenly attached the description post twice. The duplicate (promoted post `vqrfxo`) showed no delivery, so it doesn't appear to have spent. I have no tool to delete a promoted post, so it still exists in the account. It can be removed in Ads Manager.
3. **Streams are still unmeasured.** The landing page links out to streaming services, and only clicks through the link to the page can be counted here. If you want stream counts, add a pixel or UTM tags to the landing page's links to the services, or ask the streaming distributor for stream data.

**Recommendation:** The description post ("Free to stream… Ireland and the United Kingdom") and the "Halloween before plastic pumpkins" post were the best performers on link clicks, and the album announcement was the weakest. Use those two for any future campaign.

The campaign is still set to ACTIVE, but its schedule has ended, so it is no longer spending. I'll pause it if you want it closed out in the account.
